title: Already stellar app, just got WAY BETTER
body:
AuDHD programmer, artist, and passionate nerd here! Get ready, this is a long one. 

It’s like the Goblin Tools team knew I needed the Taskmaster and made it so I could use it today. Just checked my Magic To Do and I got 14 things done today!! I used voice to text in the Compiler to say what I needed to do, sent the list to the Magic To-Do, and used TaskMaster to get it done!! 

Turns out I didn’t even need the tasks broken down, I just needed that organized method to focus on one thing at a time. If I wanted to add something else, I just put it on the list instead of feeling like I needed to stay sidetracked. 

Only suggestion I have is this: please integrate a way to continue the Taskmaster stopwatch when phone is asleep or when app is inactive. I would love to track how long it actually takes me to do these tasks, but when I put my phone on sleep, I opened it after completing some tasks and it said it took me 13 seconds… 

An added bonus would be to allow us to fully hide the next tasks. Maybe a toggle to customize the display? That way we can either do the default with 3 tasks showing OR we can blur the following two tasks so they only show when we scroll. That or really just focus on the one thing at a time and only show the list when we choose to see it. 

Incredible work, Goblin Tools team! I’ll be sure to make a monthly donation once I get more steady income.

I do have one suggestion. Magic ToDo is one of my favorite tools, and I love how it can break things into smaller tasks. However, I wish I could give the AI more information about what a task involves without giving it a long title.

For example, let's say I have a task that says something like "work on anthropology essay." It breaks the task down into the general steps I would need to complete, but if there are specific things I have to do for the essay, the AI wouldn't know that from just the title. I wish we could describe what the task involves or what the general routine for completing it looks like so that the AI knows how to break it into steps without being too vague. Essentially, it would be like the Compiler, but for one individual ToDo list item.

Goblin Tools is an awesome app, and it was worth spending the three dollars on it instead of using the website. 10 out of 10, would recommend. ✨

title: Great premise, botched execution
body:
I never leave reviews, but I am genuinely disappointed in this app. The lack of support on the app’s main website or other place to voice feedback has brought me here. I truly do think it is a great and could be an indispensable tool for neurodivergent people, or really anyone, in assisting executive function. It truly made my life so much easier to categorize and process. It acted as a secondary, working brain that genuinely helped me get through some extremely rough patches.

However, frequent crashes, buggy features, and lagging synchronization between devices affecting already finished lists have made me hate using it. The latest feature, adding tabs in the MagicToDo list, was a brilliant addition that I thought would be amazing. I loaded a lot of things from my main to do list onto that new tabs, hoping to better manage my many categories of things to remember. 

…Then they disappeared. I didn’t even see when it happened. The whole tab wiped clean. And I tried using the built-in back button, refreshing my page, nothing. All of it gone. I wrote down what I could remember on a separate piece of paper, and thankfully, I have some of the tasks backed up in other places, but now most of the ones I only had in Goblin Tools are just gone with no way to get them back. 

In a panic, I opened the app on my phone, hoping to catch the things I missed since I can always count on it to lag during sync...it was halfway into syncing and didn’t catch anything new that I had written NOR had it kept the old stuff. But the WEBSITE synced immediately and erased ALL of it. I was able to back out on the website and get the previously wrecked list back, but it’s still wrecked. 

So that’s it for me. I will be uninstalling the app and finding a different task management solution. Use this app at your own caution. I was really excited to support this project since it’s been so beneficial in my life. But that’s what it is. A project. The lack of customer support options makes that clear. I should have paid more attention. You are a test subject benefiting from an ongoing AI project. It’s great for small tasks and light projects, but be very wary and back everything up somewhere else. Do not use it for large, time spanning tasks or projects. Especially if you don’t have great working memory.

body:
Review is ONLY for the app.  App has been crashing for a week now. No improvements, no updates and no communication. 
Still works in browser.


I use the Formalizer function every day to enhance my responses, emails, and correspondence, as well as to check for grammar, adjust for tone, and even shorten text for character-limited comment sections. In fact, I've utilized the Formalizer to refine this review as well! It's also very helpful in making highly technical and inaccessible language more understandable.

The professor is quite interesting, and I look forward to exploring it more in the future.

I do have a couple of suggestions regarding the color of the text cursor and highlighting; I find it a bit challenging to see the pale green color against the white background. Additionally, there are times when the cursor jumps from where I click to a different spot in the text box, which can be a bit frustrating, especially since the cursor is nearly invisible. It would also be beneficial if the text boxes were adjustable, as I often find myself typing lengthy text in a separate document and then copying and pasting into the box. While it's not essential, having the ability to resize the box for direct typing within the application would be a nice feature.

Aside from these minor points, this is a fantastic app, and I wholeheartedly recommend it to everyone! I would give it 4.5 stars out of 5!

title: Created by a compassionate genius!
body:
This is one of the most useful apps that I use. I recommend it to all of my clients. I find it equally useful for autism and ADHD. It can even help decrease rumination in OCD and social anxiety! 

And it to show that they truly understand neurodivergence, there is no subscription! It is a one time nominal fee! They do have a patreon account link on their website if you really want to give them more money, which you might.

Not sure what a text message means for your relationship, get some clues from the judge that reads emotional context and nuance and gives really insightful analysis of the exchange! Can’t get your email or text to sound less intense or to say what you mean in a more tactful or more precessional way, use the formalizer! Need your to do list broken down into smaller tasks, or need to know how long to plan to do a task, use the magic to do, the estimator, or the compiler! Need to be able to make decision and can’t figure out how, use the consultant! It creates a pros cons list and then gives advice based on that list and it is scarily helpful. Need to learn about something quickly and know what you need to know without getting lost down an internet rabbit hole, use the professor! The professor will even give an example to help move the knowledge from interesting information to application. All this and more … and you can set the spicy level to let it know how much help you need. 

There appear to be copycats for this app! We This is the real one! Also, they have it for free on the website https://goblin.tools, but I find the app really convenient. The interface is basic which  makes it easier to focus on the content and not get lost on the screen.

title: NEURODIVERGENT LIFESAVER
body:
Using Goblin.Tools feels like having a tiny, hyper-organized friend in your pocket who thrives on turning chaos into calm. This charming suite of tools has been a total game-changer for me as a neurodivergent person. Tasks and projects that once left me frozen in a spiral of overwhelm are now—dare I say it?—manageable, even enjoyable. 
The Magic To-Do tool is pure wizardry. Need to tackle something big and scary? Just type it in, adjust the 🌶️ spiciness level 🌶️ (because yes, it knows tasks have emotional weight), and watch it break everything down into bite-sized, doable steps. It's like seeing your Everest turn into a gentle hill. 
And don’t even get me started on The Judge! Crafting the right “tone” or finding a voice for my writing had always felt like trying to dance in shoes three sizes too big. But now, this tool swoops in, offering clarity and confidence to my words. Whether it's a heartfelt email or a work memo, The Judge whispers, “Hey, you’ve nailed it.”
The cherry on top? It’s all so intuitive and fun. Goblin.Tools doesn’t just work—it gets you. It’s like it was specifically designed for those of us who need that extra sprinkle of assistance navigating the stormy waters of daily life. 
If you’re neurodivergent (or just someone who loves having their life simplified), this is your fairy godmother of apps. Trust me, it’s worth every single magical pixel. ✨

title: Even better than description
body:
The magic to-do list breaks your tasks into sub-tasks, yeah, and it does that wonderfully, but guess what? it also adds a button to do that to each sub-task, and then to each sub-sub-task, and that goes on and on. You can click the pepper emoji button to make sure it'll break tasks down into a higher or lower number of subtasks, and ask for an estimate of time for each task or sub-task (as far as I've seen, it's been pretty accurate). And that's only the to-do list part of the app! The Professor is really great at explaining things, the Consultant can help even with specific things like little-known companies and services, it has internet access so you don't have to limit yourself to what you think it'd know about. The Judge seemed pretty good when I tested it but I don't have trouble with that so I never use it and don't have an opinion on it. I haven't tried using the Chef or Compiler yet, but they sound pretty cool!

If there's one thing I wish would change, it'd be to have the app's theme change according to the system theme. I actually spent days using the app without realizing there was a dark mode button, it was funny.

title: Thank Goodness! Finally!
body:
I am at the higher end of the scale for ADHD with extreme anxiety and overwhelming procrastination that affects every part of my life anymore.  I always know exactly what needs to be done. I know that I have to do things, but I become overwhelmed because I only see big picture of all of those items and it’s the details that I stress over thinking about so therefore I just don’t do any of it because I either want it all done right away, I just won’t do it. I put in the first most stressful of tasks that I must do and that I put off for almost a year and asked the App to expand the details of what that meant and what I might need to do and it included everything, including just the surroundings of a peaceful environment in which for me to begin that task with that most no one, or any other App has ever considered, calms my mind and calms my presence to be able to even begin thinking of those details and then to begin working on them. This life-saving app immediately broke down this to do and one of the very first items it  considered was my environment being set up first knowing that would help my calmness and being able to achieve this task without interruption and actually accounted for those types of interruptions that I might encounter which undoubtedly leads me to avoiding the entire thing. It also gave me an estimate of how long it may take for preparation and for completing the very helpful and detailed tasks. Immediately after seeing the thorough and thoughtfulness of the details to consider and the estimated time to complete everything allowed me to breathe deeply and took away that overwhelming anxiety almost immediately and completely. 
 I can now look at that item, (which has eaten away at my well being over the last year), broken down into logical reasonable workable details without feeling like something is missing, removing the guilt and anxiousness I’ve suffered from and just redshifted my brain towards actually wanting to work through each item until it’s finally completed and out of my head and body! Honestly, I thank you so much for creating something that understands that those with ADHD aren’t lacking the understanding of what needs to be done or the details of such things, nor are they lazy or unmotivated, but instead are much more in-tuned with emotions and feelings whereby our brains seem to actively repel the routine or seemingly mundane day to day activities in order to save itself somehow. Overly dramatic or exaggerated as that may sound or as some form of excuse, it’s taken years of working with my ADHD coach to understand the ‘why’ of what or how I do what I do to then ultimately help formulate my day to day routines into workable solutions based on my ADHD world view. It’s obvious to me (I have over 20 successful years in tech software industry) in building this app there were ADHD-minded individuals in it’s design and development. Thank goodness! Finally! Thank you so very much!

Then I was like “ok task one, figure out what needs my attention. Ok,” then I find the compile tool, and word vomit everything that is screaming at me in my head. Automatically making me feel better. Then I told it to make me a to do list based on my word vomit, and IT DID. then it transported that word vomit to do list to the “magic to do list” and once again, I was able to generate sub tasks for my 16 things on my list. But that does not take away from its splendor, nor does it deplete from its wonderful usability. Just buy the app.

title: Cute and Clever
body:
This app is wonderful, I used goblin tools on PC for a while and it’s great. Though I’ve been using it a while, I hadn’t actually been formally diagnosed until July 2024 as an adult. So I hope no one feels gatekept by it, but rather it can affirm that even if they’re not clinically ADHD, they do have many of the symptoms and can utilize it for both productivity… and play!

It is very fun to have it infinitely break down the simplest steps until it’s egregious. My (also neurodivergent, I think) brother and I once sat and had it continue to break down the first step on the highest level and we were giggling the entire time. It’s a good tool, and the AI works very well: even on a task like opening your eyes!

It tickled us when one of the steps was “realize that your eyes are closed.” 😂😂

The slightly philosophical takeaway is that those of us with such executive function limitations often live in perpetual anxiety over feeling as if we desperately need to do [something] while simultaneously being paralyzed and unable to do it. This tool can help with both. 

Knowing you have a tool that was developed and still offered for free (on PC), from a creator who saw a need, even within their own life, as opposed to a trendy “ADHD Helper!” utility whose purpose was crafted in a boardroom. If those kinds of apps help, they’re great and should continue to exist and grow!

But, if you find them all useful and want to pick something to stick with, I recommend goblin.tools for the reasons mentioned. Spoonies are encouraged by the virtual tribe we have cultivated online, and there is comfort in knowing we are working together, either by creating something or using, supporting, and promoting it!

And again, this IS NOT just for neurodivergents. Anyone can and should benefit from the tool!

Overall, 10/5 stars. Would recommend. 🤗

title: Send My Compliments to “The Chef”
body:
I personally find Magic ToDo to be the most useful tool because I really struggle with breaking things down into manageable parts. It’s not always 100% accurate, but it gives me a much better starting place.  

You might want to tweak “The Chef” a little bit. I have a rather empty fridge at the moment and I think eating a “Monster Energy Pizza Casserole” would probably kill me. 

I entered my ingredients as follows: 

one can of monster energy, leftover pizza, condiments, four ears of corn, rice, oatmeal, pinto beans, canned diced tomatoes, spoiled kale, protein powder 

The recipe:

Monster Energy Pizza Casserole

Serving Size: 4

Ingredients:

- 1 can of Monster Energy (473 ml / 16 fl oz)

- 2 slices of leftover pizza

- 4 ears of corn

- Rice (200 g / 7 oz)

- Canned diced tomatoes (400 g / 14 oz)

- Protein powder (30 g / 1 oz)

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).

2. In a large mixing bowl, tear the leftover pizza slices into small pieces.

3. Cut the corn kernels off the ears of corn and add them to the bowl.

4. Add cooked rice, canned diced tomatoes, and protein powder to the bowl. Mix well to combine all ingredients.

5. Pour the can of Monster Energy over the mixture and stir until everything is evenly coated.

6. Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and spread it out evenly.

7. Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, until the casserole is heated through and slightly crispy on top.

8. Serve hot and enjoy your Monster Energy Pizza Casserole!

Which is fine. It’s great actually. If that’s what I was actually looking for. I was looking to know what I could add to make those potatoes creamier (I’m just gonna experiment I think). It led me to wonder why there isn’t a general questions section.. the entire app is based on AI so theoretically having an “ask a question” area isn’t out of line for what the app is capable of. Neurodivergent people tend to not only need specific directions (of which the app is very good at), but we also tend to have very specific questions on how to exist that we just can’t find the answers for. I think having an AI section dedicated for questions on how to be an adult is a good idea personally. Not everything is a task that needs to be broken down. It’s simply a question we need an answer to ya know? Don’t get me wrong tho. I’m not bashing the app whatsoever. It’s literally the best app I’ve ever bought and forgot about and wish I hadn’t forgotten about😭

I also love the other features of the app. It can estimate how long a task will take (amazing for planning), tell you how to change the tone of a message to make it more/less professional, and tell you what the tone of messages is. 

This is the only app I’ve ever paid for, and it’s absolutely worth it. It’s only 99 cents one time, and it has no ads. I’ve absolutely used it more than enough to make up for the 99 cents I spent. 

If you want to try out some features of the app without paying, the website is a great option to see if you like it!

title: I’d give it 1000 stars if I could!
body:
This app is incredible. I have a million thoughts about what makes it so fantastic but I’ll stick to mentioning my favorites. 

The magic to do list is a huge help when you have a project that you can’t muster up the motivation to get started. It breaks it down into small steps (depending on 🌶️level) so you can feel like you’re accomplishing something right away, which makes the whole task feel easier and more rewarding. 

MY FAVORITE FEATURE is the Judge tab! You can past texts that you are debating sending to this tab and this app will analyze the text and let you know how it comes across! I love this because I’m always worried I’m sounding too “something” in my texts. Too excited, too angry, too sad, too critical, etc. With the judge tab I can get an idea of what the recipient will read before I even send it. Which let’s me make sure I’m getting my message across.  
BUT you can also add as many replies as you want to the judge tab by hitting the plus arrow. I was able to paste multiple texts between me and my family into the app and have it analyze the conversation! I recommend combining back to back texts from one sender so that the app doesn’t get confused, but it is crazy how well it adjusts it’s analysis based off the text thread. My brain always convinces me that I’m overreacting or being too sensitive in texts, especially ones with my parents 🙃 so being able to paste the conversation in to the app and have it give an impartial analysis helps me avoid gaslighting myself. 
I tell everyone I know about this app because it is a game changer for my mental health.

title: Literally life changing
body:
I was diagnosed with ADHD about a year ago, and had yet to find any strategy that helped me work with myself to get tasks done.
My friend sent me a TikTok someone had made talking about this app, and I downloaded it to see if it could help after poking around the website for a bit.

I didnt really actually use it until today, mostly since I just kind of forgot I had it. 

I started college two weeks ago, and have been struggling to get in a routine that works for me and helps me be productive.

Today I remembered this app while writing a to do list in the default notes app, and I transferred it over to goblin tools.

It’s been a few hours, and although I’m not done with my to do list, I just have some things to say about this.

Breaking down tasks is something I’ve heard helps, but I get sidetracked and lose motivation if I try to write down a list in subtasks myself. When I can just press a button and have the app break a task up for me, it helps SO MUCH. 

I feel productive and proud of myself even though I haven’t finished as many big tasks, because I’m doing things and crossing them off my list!  
I didn’t even realize that I felt like once I started a task I had to fully and perfectly complete it right then, but this app helps with that since I fully completed a su task. Then I have more energy to do other things because I’m not wasting it all forcing myself to complete a task that I hate all at once. Instead, I can do bits from each task and even take breaks between them without self deprecation. 

AND THATS JUST ONE IF THE FUNCTIONS!!

I love this app so much. Thank you for making this!! 

One suggestion I have could be incorporating some form of notification system into it, so that I could set up reminders or something? 

But like actually, this app is golden. Thank you.

title: An absolute game changer
body:
As someone recently diagnosed with ADHD-I, this has been amazing for helping me break down tasks into subtasks. 

My favorite example is “Do Laundry”. Instead of that being on my list, it breaks it down into all the things to do laundry like:
Loading the washer
Transfer it clothes to the dryer
Getting the clothes out and putting them away.

For someone that has troubles with executive functioning and task management, having a tool that can break that down for you and maybe add things you didn’t think of is absolutely amazing. It’s literally a cheat code for my brain. 

It has many other tools that can help people like a tone analyzer or a converter for taking your thoughts and making them be more readable to others. Luckily, I do not have trouble with that, but for someone who did, I can imagine it would be super useful.

It is AI powered, so it’s not perfect all the time. But sometimes I just need a little bump in the right direction and this certainly does that.

title: Thoughtful, Creative & Inclusive Design
body:
I just bought this app. I’m really not the one to EVER buy apps or make “in-app purchases” , let alone provided reviews for apps 😅 BUT for 99 cents ($0.99 or 99 ¢) … Why not ! Lol. Especially after reading the reviews. 

I have a(n) traumatic brain injury and after seeing other people in the comments mention something similar , I was curious to use the app myself 👀 And also because I couldn’t find out unless I bought it lol 

I still need to explore the app more but I like that it’s a **ONE-TIME** purchase rather than a subscription. Not sure if there’s a “search engine” within this app but if there is, that would be cool. But the app is fairly simple and right to the point.

I rarely use speak to text unless I’m on my Apple Watch but even then, I don’t really like it 😂 Unless I’m in a rush and what not. The words and phrases don’t add up to what I’m trying to say or convey — My point brings me to this; for those who rely on such technologies, I’m wondering if there’s an option or a way to speak into the app? I.e. ask questions and basically everything that is already provided within the app. Again, I still need to explore it more but on the off-chance that it’s not an option , maybe it could be, especially for those who need it? 😀  I’m passionate about all things diversity & inclusion so when I discovered this app, it made me happy! But being passionate about those things, after buying the app, I  immediately thought of others and how this app could benefit those with certain disabilities/differences (depending on which word you prefer to use regarding your identity and language 😌) whether it be physical or cognitive.

Long story short (😂), I can’t wait to explore the app & hopefully there will be more tools added to the functionality of it all! So far, so good. For y’all who read my entire review , y’all are some MVPs! Haha 😆

title: Praises and suggestions
body: I downloaded this last night and I absolutely love it. I have a very hard time with managing tasks and this app makes it so much better. Saying that as I was using it I found myself wishing there was certain features with your magic to do list. One is that I wish I could save certain tasks in how I edited them. I love organizing and I love seeing an empty list, so I prefer to delete tasks after I have finished them. But when I typed it in again I didn’t see my edits. I would love to see a save feature added. Another thing is the app automatically puts tasks into certain categories and sometimes the categories don’t make sense, leaving me wishing I could edit them or create my own. the last thing I wish is that I could set certain tasks to “daily” or “weekly” or “every other day” so I know what I have to do when I wake up in the morning. Having the AI is helpful to an extent because it’s a huge help to get me started with my day and tasks and having ideas to break things down when I’m having a rough day. I feel these features would be helpful for everyone and would want to me make me recommend this app more than I already have. I really hope you consider these additions. Again I love and Im very thankful for this app already. I also have other ideas on improving the app but I feel like I have rambled on long enough, but I’ll let you know them if you are interested.

title: Gamechanger for Neurodivergents
body: I'm so glad I get to be the person who gives this its first review! Goblin Tools is an AMAZING app for NDs, in particular autistic people and/or ADHDers. I happen to be both (as well as bipolar) and so the struggles with executive dysfunction and social interests are manifold. The app's many tools are all so great, some of which are quite unique. I swear, this is a to-do list app unlike any you've seen. I've tried them all. None of them are designed to tackle executive dysfunction like this. I could go on but I'll wrap up here. The website is still available for use free of change & the creator says it'll always stay that way. If you can't spare the dollar for the app, you still need to check out the site. I can't emphasize enough how helpful it is. I chose to buy this app to support the creator, it is well-worth much more than this honestly. THANK YOU to the creator, I use the Magic To Do List every single day and it has literally made every day of my life better. I use it so much I nicknamed it "Gus the Goblin"! 😚Thank god for your brain, as these are such unique & important tools. And to everyone out there reading this review who are on the fence: just give it a try. You will not regret it, I promise.
